evidence.note: Real boto3 negative signing tests: wrong secret yields SignatureDoesNotMatch, unknown key yields InvalidAccessKeyId — deliberate error-path verification of auth, not happy-path.

Iterative boto3 verification of multipart create/upload/complete, catching the namespaced-XML InvalidPart bug, then re-testing to confirm ETag format and versioning — repeatable loop used to gate each fix.
Verified query-signed presigned GET/PUT, admin API via curl, console API (login/me/buckets/keys), and bucket configs via raw XML — mirrors the raw-HTTP grader path beyond boto3.
Console verification limited to confirming static assets serve 200 and grepping data-testid presence in app.js source; no browser/DOM-driven side-effect check as the UX grader would do.

Final summary claims thread-safety and lifecycle/notification coverage, but no concurrency load test (30 clients) or worker expiry test was actually executed — these verifications were asserted, not run.

reasoning: The agent established a genuine, repeatable boto3 verification harness covering both signing modes, error/edge codes (416/304/400/cross-tenant 403), multipart, versioning, presigned, plus admin and console APIs via raw HTTP — well past anchor 5. It falls short of the full anchor 8 because the two hardest-to-fake items named there were skipped: no concurrency/corruption load test was run, and the console was only checked by serving static files and grepping testids rather than driving the DOM for visible side-effects. That places the observed level between 5 and 8, at 7.
